hero.heading: What is Sankofa?
hero.intro: A word from the Akan people of Ghana that carries a whole philosophy: return to your roots, recover what is valuable, and carry it forward.

meaning.translation: “It is not taboo to go back and fetch what is at risk of being left behind.”

chapters.heading: A proverb of wisdom
chapters.body: Sankofa comes from the Twi language of the Akan people of Ghana and Côte d'Ivoire. It teaches that the past is not a burden to escape but a source of knowledge. Whatever we have lost, forgotten or been forced to give up can be reclaimed — and reclaiming it is how we move forward with purpose.

chapters.heading: The bird that looks back
chapters.body: Sankofa is drawn as a bird whose feet face forward while its head turns back, carrying a precious egg in its beak. The egg is the future; the backward glance is memory. It is also written as a heart-shaped Adinkra symbol, one of the visual proverbs printed on cloth, carved in wood and cast in gold across West Africa.

chapters.heading: A symbol of the diaspora
chapters.body: Across the African diaspora, Sankofa has become a symbol of reclaimed history and cultural pride — a reminder that the struggles and triumphs of those who came before us light the path ahead.

whyHeading: Why our awards carry this name
whyBody: The Sankofa Royale Awards look back to honour the people who built our communities, and forward to inspire those who will lead them next. Each award is a small act of Sankofa: going back to fetch the stories, sacrifices and successes that might otherwise be forgotten, and lifting them up for everyone to see.

values.title: Remember
values.text: Honour heritage, elders and the foundations they laid.

values.title: Recognise
values.text: Celebrate excellence that too often goes unseen.

values.title: Rise
values.text: Carry the lessons forward to build what comes next.
